reasoning:
**What is asked.** The number of MPs voting *for* no confidence in PM Anutin Charnvirakul at the first such vote before 23 December 2026. No vote in time resolves as "140 or fewer".

**Starting point.** The opposition filed its motion on 8 October with 145 MP signatures (Nation Thailand, 8 and 28 Oct; ACLED, 15 Oct). Reuters (3 Nov) counts 292 coalition seats in a 499-member House and 207 outside it, including Kla Tham's 58 MPs, who did not sign. By my arithmetic that leaves 149 MPs in the five opposition parties: People's 120, Democrat 21, Thai Ruam Palang 6, Thai Liberal 1 and Thai Pakdee 1. So about four did not sign. From memory of earlier Thai censure votes, the tally against a prime minister lands at or a few votes under the signing bloc, because small parties and defectors peel away.

**Evidence.**
- Government and opposition whips agreed a debate on 7-10 December and a vote on 11 December (Nation, 28 Oct; Reuters, 3 Nov). The session runs to 22 December. The Nation's latest censure item (14 Nov) has Anutin preparing his answers, with no sign of a change. I put "no vote in time" near 4%.
- In the 19 March vote for prime minister, Thai Ruam Palang's six MPs and one People's MP backed Anutin (Wikipedia, Second Anutin cabinet). Those six are the swing: with them the tally sits around 145-148, without them around 141-143.
- Reports expect Kla Tham to be brought into government after the debate (Thairath, 21 Oct; Bangkok Biznews, 28 Oct), so I expect it to stay out of the no-confidence column.

**What would give another outcome.** Thai Ruam Palang switching sides plus a few absences, a Democrat abstention, a walkout or a postponement past 22 December gives 140 or fewer. All 149 holding, or stray coalition votes, gives 149-154. Kla Tham or Pheu Thai turning on Anutin gives 155 or more.

**Forecast.** 140 or fewer 17%, 141-144 29%, 145-148 41%, 149-154 9%, 155 or more 4%.
question_title: How many votes of no confidence will Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul receive?
